metadata.I: "Battle Birds of the Quantum Realm: Odin’s Saga"
metadata.II: First, a three-year summer, then a three-year winter, and then war as a result of deflation and famine. Brother fights brother for the little that's left. The mountains collapse, and the giant women fall helplessly into the sea and sink. The Fenrisulven breaks free, now that the mountains to which he was attached are no more, and swallows the sun; the wolf's time reigns.
metadata.III: In this time of chaos, Odin needed help, which is why he released his ravens, Hugin and Munin, to see what the world was missing. The two ravens returned: "A new time is about to prevail, a time in which everyone can travel over the world like Sleipnir, a world in which each can take a different shape like you, Odin," replied the ravens.
metadata.IV: Odin pondered for nine days and nine nights before he came to a solution on how he would confront Ragnarök by cleverly gathering the knowledge of the entire universe in one and the same form. "I'm going to create and expose my warriors to The Quantum Rift, with a massive influx of ancient knowledge and encrypted data, which will be scattered throughout the nine worlds and back to Valhalla."
metadata.V: "My warriors will fight the Fenrisulven, the Vanalands, or anything else that comes their way. I will equip them with intelligence that the world has never seen before. I will let them fight battles and learn from their mistakes, so that we can save ourselves from the end of the world. Let the battle begin!"

metadata.description: Why did we create bucket NFT? Well, a lot of folks are camera shy and struggle with social anxiety, while many girls feel uncomfortable taking photos without makeup. That's where our bucket NFT comes in—to empower everyone to share photos and videos on social media confidently, without worrying about showing their faces and overcoming social anxiety! MenderNFT used to hang out on the ETH mainnet. We led the Bucket People to craft the MenderFinance tool, explored the Cryptovoxels metaverse, produced the Bucket video MenderShow, and even dipped our toes into TikTok with Bucket short videos. And you know what? We're not slowing down. We're diving into the Bitcoin ecosystem now, and a bunch of introverted Bucket community members are starting to wrap their heads around Ordinals and Rune!

Welcome esteemed collectors and connoisseurs of Bitcoin history to the exclusive collection of the original two large pizzas purchased with the first-ever Bitcoin transaction, now preserved for posterity. This historic moment, marking the genesis of Bitcoin's real-world utility, is encapsulated within these slices, making them not just technological artifacts but veritable icons of the blockchain revolution.  Quantity: Two large pizzas, each divided into 8 individual slices.  Provenance: These pizzas were originally bought by Laszlo Hanyecz from Jeremy Sturdivant on May 22, 2010, for 10,000 Bitcoins, now hailed as one of the most legendary transactions in the cryptocurrency world and of all human history.  Preservation: Meticulously preserved using state-of-the-art techniques to maintain their original form and integrity, ensuring a timeless link to Bitcoin's infancy.  There are only 16 original Historic Bitcoin Pizza Slices, and each slice has been carefully inscribed onto the exact same rare satoshis from the original 10,000 BTC pizza transaction.  Certification: Authenticated by the Bitcoin blockchain itself, affirming their exact location of inscription on the real Bitcoin pizza transaction satoshis and genuine connection to the genesis of Bitcoin commerce.  Display: Housed in a bespoke showcase display featuring a beautiful and timeless black background, these slices are ready to take pride of place in the collection of the most discerning Bitcoin enthusiast.

metadata.description: Why did we create bucket NFT? Well, a lot of folks are camera shy and struggle with social anxiety, while many girls feel uncomfortable taking photos without makeup. That's where our bucket NFT comes in—to empower everyone to share photos and videos on social media confidently, without worrying about showing their faces and overcoming social anxiety! MenderNFT used to hang out on the ETH mainnet. We led the Bucket People to craft the MenderFinance tool, explored the Cryptovoxels metaverse, produced the Bucket video MenderShow, and even dipped our toes into TikTok with Bucket short videos. And you know what? We're not slowing down. We're diving into the Bitcoin ecosystem now, and a bunch of introverted Bucket community members are starting to wrap their heads around Ordinals and Rune!

8,765. Disguised Him.Description: The Currency, launched in July 2021, is a collection of 10,000 NFTs which correspond with 10,000 original artworks by Damien Hirst. Collectors were given the choice to either keep the NFT or exchange it for the physical artwork. Every choice made – to keep the NFT, or keep the painting – had consequences. Collectors that chose to claim a physical artwork had to burn their NFT to do so. Similarly, those who chose to keep their NFT did so knowing that the physical artwork would then be destroyed. The exchange period closed on 27 July 2022 resulting in just over half the collectors (5,149) deciding to keep the physical artwork, and 4,851 to keep the NFT.

metadata.The Assumption: Adamma: In this piece, I replace Guercino’s Virgin Mary with the southeastern Nigerian masquerade called “Adamma” – who is an embodiment of femininity even though it is always a man behind the mask. The “assumption” or, if you will, “ascension” of Adamma is a reminder that she is just as culturally relevant as globally known characters like Barney, Big Bird, Teletubbies, Mickey Mouse, Kermit the Frog, and Winnie-the-Pooh – except that her pop culture potential has remained untapped. These other characters surround her in the same spots where Guercino painted the angels and little cherubs surrounding the Virgin Mary, as they lift her towards the heavens.

metadata.Artwork description: Magnolia illustrates 4032 hand-embroidered cotton stitches on a grid-based cotton cloth canvas. Embedded within the geometric abstraction is a cryptographic aleatoric notation, derived from the rhythmic biodata of the magnolia, recognized as one of the first flowering plants during the cretaceous period 100 million years ago.  The magnolia is a primordial bloom that carries with it wisdom and robust perseverance due to its existence within and throughout deep time.  To retrieve the biodata of the magnolia, sensors are directly attached to the plant to record the changes in electrical conductivity that transpire through the stomata. The stomata is a direct channel between the plants’ internal autonomous systems and the conditions of the external world. Each time a significant change occurs within the stomata, this activity is communicated and recorded to the sensor. This biodata is then sonified and generated into a rhythm that ascribes 1/8th note and rest values, with the onset of each coloured line indicating the duration of each 1/8th note.  Conforming to the principles of aleatoric composition, the rhythm relies on chance and randomness determined by the magnolia's disposition at the time of recording.  The stitches articulate a rule-based compositional procedure that notate the “beat” of the magnolia, effectively putting a stable frame around an autonomous system in flux, lending material expression to contingencies that constitute the world external to the magnolia.   The choice of stitching with two colour values, nods to the bedrock of computer language, base-2, in which only two values are utilized to constitute conversation, or in this case, rhythmic notation.  The textural low-relief of embroidery encourages touch and tangibility of the digitally recorded provenance, crafting the concept of stitching as storage, wherein textiles store, index, and arrange data in meaningful ways that allow us to access and recite ephemeral data.   The artwork is inscribed on sat # 1945185800000000 (Aug 9, 2023, 11:56 AM), a sat from the day the magnolia biodata was originally obtained.
